title: Consolidate pre-install probe templates and introduce tenant-scoped init-rate profiles
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add tenant-scoped init-rate profiles and unified pre-install probe templates. Backwards-compatible values; adds migration guide and example values for Private installs.
description:
Context: Private installer customers run into protracted cluster preflight phases when multi-tenant on-prem installs execute large numbers of tenant init jobs concurrently. This causes API server saturation and sporadic timeouts during pre-install health checks.

Motivation: provide a safer, opt-in default for helm charts that (1) centralizes pre-install and readiness probe templates to reduce duplication, (2) exposes tenant-scoped init-rate profiles (concurrency + burst) so operators can trade install speed for API stability, and (3) add a lightweight migration path so existing values are not broken.

Checklist:
- [x] Add unified probe template library for preflight and init jobs
- [x] Introduce tenant.initRateProfiles map in values.yaml with profiles (low/medium/high)
- [x] Implement values merging precedence and deprecation warnings
- [x] Add integration tests for staggered init behavior and preflight liveness
- [x] Documentation: update values.example and migration guide
- [x] CI: lint, unit tests, helm template, and an e2e job that runs a 6-tenant dry-run

Changes (high level):
- chart/templates/_probes.tpl: new consolidated probe helper (preflightProbe, initLiveness, initReadiness) that takes profile and overrides
- chart/values.schema.json: extended schema for tenant.initRateProfiles and probeOverrides with strict types and examples
- chart/values.example.yaml: new examples showing per-tenant overrides and recommended profiles
- chart/templates/init-job.yaml: wiring to read initRateProfile and apply rate controller annotations (init.kubernetes.io/concurrency, init.kubernetes.io/burst)
- chart/templates/preflight-hook.yaml: use preflightProbe helper and dynamically compute timeouts based on profile
- scripts/migrate-values.sh: helper that rewrites deprecated top-level initRate fields into the new tenant-scoped map (used in upgrade notes)
- tests/helm/staggered-init.test.yaml: unit-style helm template test showing annotation presence for each profile

Commits:
- 9c3f7d8 Add probe template helpers and initial tests
- b14a0fe Add tenant.initRateProfiles schema and example values
- e2f4c1a Wire init-job and preflight-hook to profile annotations and timeouts; add migrate-values script
- 4f5b2d0 Fix: revert flaky e2e timeout and tune medium profile
- d3a71b2 Docs: write migration guide and values examples

Files touched (selective):

Testing & CI:
- Local lint + helm template passed
- Unit-style Helm tests (kubeval + schema checks) added and passed in CI
- E2E job initially failed due to tight timeouts; fixed by adjusting medium profile defaults and rerunning.

Final CI: all checks green (lint, unit, helm-template, e2e-dryrun).

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco Chen (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Two asks: 1) make sure default medium profile is conservative for older clusters, 2) add a clear deprecation message in values.schema.json for the old initRate keys."
- Author (Aisha): "Addressed both: medium profile defaults dialed back (see commit b14a0fe) and deprecation warnings added in schema and migration script."
- Lena Fischer (reviewer): "Can we add a knob to completely opt-out of the rate controller annotations for customers who use external init orchestration?"
- Author: "Added tenant.initRateProfiles.<profile>.enabled boolean and documented opt-out in values.example.yaml."
- Diego Alvarez (approver): "Verified on internal testbed with 8 tenants, medium profile helps prevent apiserver saturation. Approving for merge."

Migration notes for operators:
- This change is backwards-compatible: existing top-level initRate fields are still supported but deprecated. Use scripts/migrate-values.sh to automatically convert to the new tenant.initRateProfiles map during upgrades.
- Default behavior: if tenant-specific profile not supplied, chart falls back to global initRate profile, then to 'medium' safe defaults.
- If you previously relied on aggressive concurrency, review new 'high' profile and adjust quotas accordingly.

Observability:
- Added two new Helm chart metrics labels for init profile (chart.k8s.redwood/init_profile) so Console dashboards can correlate init-phase latency with configured profiles.

Security and compliance:
- No secrets introduced. Rate-control annotations are purely metadata; no RBAC changes required.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged via GitHub web UI after approvals (merge method: squash).

Post-merge follow-ups:
- ENG-1248 follow-up created to evaluate adaptive-init autoscaler in next sprint
- Documentation PR queued to redwood-docs that imports values.example snippets and upgrade instructions

Notes: kept changes intentionally conservative to avoid surprises for Private customers running in constrained air-gapped environments. The migration script is minimal and prints a dry-run by default.
